sections.content:
主题：用Excel做各种项目。

知识技能：包括行列计算，蒙特卡洛模拟，规划求解等等。大概半个学期在学习规划求解，内容由易到难，处理不同情境的问题。

there is no listed content provided by Coach Zhang, but basically all teaching will surrounding excel solver.

At the beginning of semester he will teach some basic techniques of excel (conditional formatting, functions, random...etc)
Then jump into solver part, mostly using solver to solve simultaneous problems.
For the quiz, there are three questions also about solver, its easy if you can think of the logic behind.
After the quiz, coach Zhang will introduce matrix functions (no need to understand complicated concepts, just know how to use will be good)
Also including this function into Solver, but one thing to know is that solver cannot process functions in the calculations therefore there are some new techniques on how to use it properly. the techniques are not hard actually, but the logic behind requires you to think of, it will be very difficult to 死記硬背.

Overall, it is not hard for the content itself, more than it, the logic thinking will be much more difficult.

sections.content: The content is interesting. For those who did A level Maths, it's like the excel version of the Decisions 1 paper. The content is highly diverse and ranges from personal finance planning to HR planning to operational planning. The course largely revolves around the solver function in Excel. It's a feature that allows you to do linear optimisation and a majority of the course is about how to model questions in a way that allows you to use the solver to reach a solution.
sections.teaching:
I liked Professor Zhang's teaching, it was interactive and highly appropriate for an excel course. In the first lesson he said his course is a lot more like a workshop than a lecture. However, I found his pace to be rather militant and if you're not able to keep up it's hard to catch up during the lecture. Prof Zhang did make an effort to accommodate to students who don't understand such as by asking if anyone has questions etc but it's just hard because of the nature of the lecture and I assume the culture regarding participation in classrooms in HK.

For me I found the best to be to watch his lecture videos and follow along with your excel open step by step. That way you can enjoy the interactive follow-along nature of his workshop while being able to pause and rewind whenever you feel like you didn't understand.
sections.grading:
The course had one quiz and one final. If you did better on the final than the quiz your grade would be 100% based on the final exam.

Prof Zhang did not post any statistics for any of the quiz or exam.
Overall, I scored 85/100 on the Final and 18/100 on the quiz. My final letter grade was A.
sections.workload: I found this course to be very traditional in the sense that there was only one quiz (basically a midterm) and one final. It felt a lot like a high-school exam and honestly made it a lot more simpler to learn and study. Either you know the content or you don't, you don't need to worry about group projects or homework's that are going to be AI anyways.

sections.content:
# Useful and handful excel stuff including common excel functions and excel solver

# Applications to solving managerial decision problems in diverse industries and functional areas will be discussed, including
- Operations Management: logistics and supply chains management; airline flight scheduling; airline hub location; process flow management.
- Finance and accounting: breakeven analysis; investment analysis; loan portfolio planning; pension fund planning; portfolio selection.
- Human resources: workforce scheduling; sales territory assignment and sales-force allocation.

sections.teaching:

sections.grading:
# Two Quizzes, 20% each; Final 60%

# You cannot miss more than three classes after add-drop period, even though there is no attendance component. 1 mark will be deducted for exceeding the upper bound.

# If you do better on the final exam than on the quiz, he will shift the weight of each quiz, 20%, to the final exam. Therefore, the weight of final exam could be 80% or 100% as well. However, in general the average exam score will be lower than the average quiz score.

# There are FIVE questions in the final exam, 20 points each. The below is the knowledge or skills covered in each question (Can't remember all the details):
1. Basic Excel function
- Data Validation
- INDEX(), MATCH()
- Absolute reference, Relative reference
- CORREL(),COVARIANCE.P()
2. Random Sequence
- RAND(), RANK()
- COUNTIFS()
- How to create a data-table with 1000 samples
3-5. Excel solver with three different levels
- Easy: Basic constraints type
- Intermediate: Cumulative demand and supply
- Difficult: Logical bounds and multiple changing variables. For this one, I still don't know how to quickly think of the solution to this type of problem.

sections.content:
A useful course on spreadsheet modeling with Microsoft Excel. We're first introduced with basic Excel tools formulae and tools such as VLOOKUP, PivotTable and Data Table. It then moves to building spreadsheet models for different business scenarios. A significant proportion of the course (Chapters 3 - 7) focuses on optimization modeling with Solver. The problem-solving approach of this course is really great. It allows us to learn not just the Excel features, but also the way to model and solve various business problems.

Topics included:
 Introduction to Management Science
 Introduction to Spreadsheet Modeling
 Introduction to Optimization Modeling
 Linear Programming Models
 Network Models
 Optimization Models with Integer Variables
 Nonlinear Optimization Models
sections.teaching: Prof ZHENG has a mild mainland accent, but this does not really affect our understanding. His pace of speech is perfect and we can easily follow his teaching. He's also a responsible instructor, willing to reply emails and answer our inquiries within a short period of time.
sections.grading:
Assessment Scheme:
 20% In-class quiz
 10% Assignments
 64% Final exam
 6% Class attendance
 +5% Bonus for class participation/discussion

I got 95/100 in the quiz (mean = 89.2), 92/100 in the final (mean = 75.2), full marks in the assignments and class attendance.

 Final grade: A

Fair enough.
sections.workload:
There are a total of 3 assignments on business cases extracted from the textbook. We're required to form groups of 1 to 3, and answer the questions by building Excel spreadsheet models from scratch. The business cases are not easy and we deffo need to spend some time on them. But this is reasonable considering that it's a 4-credit course.

Both the quiz and the final are computer-based exams similar to the exercises done in class in terms of format. The quiz covers chapters 2 to 3, while the final covers chapters 3 to 7. Open books, open notes, and we're provided with the PowerPoint slides. Make sure you prepare well for the final as it's more difficult, and it takes a huge chunk of your grade. Pay special attention to the tricks of how to transform a nonlinear model to a linear model.

sections.content:
This course mainly focuses on optimisation, problem solving and decision making. Rather than focusing specific theories or frameworks (like you would encounter in most of the other courses), the professor introduces various problems each class, and the class time is spent in thinking about how to solve these problems logically, and then using Excel (and related Excel functions like Solver) to solve these problems.

For people who like studying out a textbook with a clear syllabus and topic list, I think this course will be quite interesting (and challenging) in the beginning, since there are no lecture notes provided, per say.

The content itself is very interesting, and you get to learn a lot about different Excel features and functions (I certainly learnt a lot of useful functions). A lot of the things you learn can be applied in various other courses, like workforce scheduling, production optimisation, logistics, etc.

As a required course for the OM major, I would definitely say that the course is quite fascinating, practical and useful.
sections.teaching: Professor Zhang is a very friendly and helpful professor, and he's very willing to answer any questions you may have (through email or face-to-face). Initially, you might find the style of teaching a bit different, as you spend the entire lesson going through 4-5 Excel files and solving various problems. If you can get used to this style of learning, then I find that you will definitely be able to appreciate Prof. Zhang's teaching.
sections.grading:
Grading is relatively fair.

The final grade is made up of two major components
— Quizzes (3 quizzes, 15% each)
— Final Exam (55%)

The quizzes are held in-class and contain relatively short problems (it's hard to predict what the problems will be).

The final exam is much tougher and requires much more thinking, and it can cover anything taught in the course.

You can skip all of the quizzes and shift the entire weighting of the course to the final exam, the professor is very flexible with this.
sections.workload: The workload really depends on the grade you want. There are no homework assignments or projects due. The professor does upload 3 exercises (for the whole semester), but these are optional - although it's a good idea to complete these exercises since they are a good way to practice your skills.
